<thought>Based on the observed mass spectrum, the most distinctive isotopic pattern is the M+2 peak at ≈ 237 m/z with an intensity of about 4–5 % of the base peak (235 m/z). This relative intensity matches the natural abundance of ³⁴S (≈ 4.2 % of total sulfur). No M+2 peak with ~33 % intensity (characteristic of chlorine) or ~100 % intensity (characteristic of bromine) is present, and the M+1 peak (~16 % of the base) does not correspond to the typical ~1 % for ¹³C‑enriched patterns in a single element. Therefore, the only element whose isotopic signature can be definitively identified from the spectrum is sulfur. 

The final answer is a list containing just that element. 
</thought>
<final_answer>['S']</final_answer>
